title: A 71 m Buddha in a Cliff: River View or Climb to Its Feet? | China Travel Expert
description:
Carved straight into a riverside cliff in Sichuan, the Leshan Giant Buddha is about 71 metres tall — the largest pre-modern stone Buddha in the world. Monks began the carving around 713 AD, and it took roughly 90 years to finish.

The clever part is hidden: a network of drainage channels tucked into the hair, the collar and behind the ears carries rainwater away, and it has helped the statue resist erosion for over 1,200 years.

There are two classic ways to meet it: a boat on the river that shows you the full scale, or the steep cliff stairway that brings you down level with its feet.

★ Expert Tip: the cliff staircase gets long queues on weekends and holidays — go on a weekday morning, or take the river boat if you want the whole Buddha in one frame.

乐山大佛：约 71 米高，唐代开凿，藏在发高、衣领里的排水槽让它立了一千两百年。坐船看全貌，或走栩道到脚下——你选哪个？
